subject: math

objective.text: Estimate lengths with mental benchmarks. Then measure to check your estimate.

explanations.title: Mental benchmarks
explanations.text: A mental benchmark is an object you know the length of. Use it to think about other lengths. A quarter is about an inch. A sheet of paper is about a foot. A door width is about a yard.

explanations.title: Estimate, then measure
explanations.text: Step 1: Pick a mental benchmark and estimate. Step 2: Measure to see how close you are.

explanations.title: Compare to the benchmark
explanations.text: Find the benchmark closest in length to the object. Is the object a little more or a little less? A lot more or a lot less?

explanations.title: Picture the benchmark again and again
explanations.text: See how many times the benchmark fits along the object. That helps you estimate the length.

explanations.title: Why benchmarks help
explanations.text: If someone says a room is about 10 yards long, a benchmark helps you picture it. Benchmarks help you understand sizes.

examples.title: Estimate a marker
examples.text: Estimates for the marker: 7 inches and 5 inches. The marker is shorter than the paper but longer than a quarter. You measure it. It is 8 inches.

examples.title: Benjamin's arms
examples.text: Forearm is 15 inches. Upper arm is 15 inches. One arm is 15 plus 15, which is 30 inches. Both arms are 30 plus 30, which is 60 inches.
